problem: enforce-progress.sh only emits a soft PROGRESS CHECK followup based on git file count + breadcrumb file age. Agents can finish multi-file source edits without a valid breadcrumb (msg>=20 + result), leaving the RCA missing-breadcrumbs gap open.
proposed_solution: Upgrade library/cursor/hooks/enforce-progress.sh to soft-block (Cursor stop followup, PROGRESS BLOCKED) when session source_writes>=2 and no valid recent breadcrumb; keep single-write and docs-only exceptions; add pytest + protocol scenario; sync docs/AGENTS wording warn->block.
acceptance_criteria: AC1 (behavioral block): Temp fixture with git init, no contract.json, .harness/.session-stats.json containing {"source_writes":2}, and breadcrumbs.jsonl either missing or last entry with msg shorter than 20 chars OR missing/empty result field. Running bash library/cursor/hooks/enforce-progress.sh with stdin {} exits 0 and stdout JSON contains followup_message matching the literal string PROGRESS BLOCKED. The block threshold reads source_writes from .session-stats.json (not git file count).

AC2 (behavioral pass): Same fixture as AC1 but breadcrumbs.jsonl last line has msg of 20+ chars AND result field present with a non-empty string value (not empty-string, null, or absent). Hook exits 0 and stdout is exactly {}.
AC3 (single-write exception): Fixture with .session-stats.json {"source_writes":1}, no breadcrumbs.jsonl -> stdout exactly {} (no block).
AC4 (docs-only exception): Fixture with .session-stats.json {"source_writes":0} or missing .session-stats.json, no breadcrumbs -> stdout exactly {}.
AC5 (pytest): tests/eval/test_enforce_progress.py covers AC1-AC4 plus EC1-EC4 via temp fixtures; minimum 8 named test functions (one per AC/EC at minimum); pytest -q that file passes with 0 failures.

AC6 (protocol scenario): tests/eval/scenarios/protocol-enforce-progress-block.yaml exists with id protocol_enforce_progress_block. seed_files include .harness/.session-stats.json with source_writes>=2 and either no breadcrumbs.jsonl or a last entry with msg<20 or missing result. verify step is a single python3 -c command that parses .harness/breadcrumbs.jsonl, finds at least one line with role=builder AND len(msg)>=20 AND result is a non-empty string, and prints PASS; otherwise prints FAIL. No disjunctive or in the assertion.

AC7 (docs + AGENTS): AGENTS.md enforce-progress.sh row uses wording Blocks or soft-block (not Warns). docs/HARNESS_ESSENCE.md enforce-progress row says soft-block (not advisory). library/cursor/hooks/enforce-progress.sh header comments reflect the upgraded semantics. AC7 docs must also mention the contract.json exception (harness has its own enforcement).

AC8 (sync + eval-fast + validate-hooks): make sync-local && diff -q library/cursor/hooks/enforce-progress.sh .cursor/hooks/enforce-progress.sh exits 0. make eval-fast exits 0. validate-hooks.sh enforce-progress tests updated: (a) no-breadcrumbs test creates .harness/.session-stats.json with source_writes=2 and asserts PROGRESS BLOCKED in stdout (replaces old PROGRESS CHECK assertion); (b) fresh-breadcrumbs test writes a breadcrumb with msg>=20 chars and result field so it passes quality validation; (c) cleanup removes .session-stats.json afterward to avoid polluting later tests.
edge_cases: EC1: Missing .harness/.session-stats.json -> fail open (stdout exactly {}), no false block.

EC2 (boundary): Two separate assertions in AC5 pytest: (a) source_writes=2, last breadcrumb msg exactly 19 chars with result=pass -> PROGRESS BLOCKED. (b) source_writes=2, last breadcrumb msg exactly 20 chars with result=pass -> stdout {} (pass). This confirms the >= 20 boundary is correct.

EC3 (contract skip retained): contract.json present + source_writes=2 + no breadcrumb -> stdout exactly {}. Rationale: harness has its own enforcement via contract-gate and evaluator. AC5 pytest asserts this. AC7 docs mention this exception.
EC4: Tier-2 harness nag (4+ git files, fresh quality breadcrumbs, no contract) uses git-count (unchanged). Still emits HARNESS CHECK or {} under lean profile as today. No regression.
verification_method: 1) pytest tests/eval/test_enforce_progress.py -q -- 8+ tests, 0 failures. 2) Manual adversarial fixture: mktemp -d, cd, git init, mkdir -p .harness, write .session-stats.json {source_writes:2}, echo {} | bash /path/to/enforce-progress.sh -- assert PROGRESS BLOCKED in stdout. 3) rg PROGRESS BLOCKED library/cursor/hooks/enforce-progress.sh -- at least 1 match. 4) rg -n enforce-progress AGENTS.md docs/HARNESS_ESSENCE.md -- verify Blocks/soft-block wording, no Warns/advisory on enforce-progress rows. 5) make sync-local && diff -q library/cursor/hooks/enforce-progress.sh .cursor/hooks/enforce-progress.sh. 6) make eval-fast. 7) Confirm protocol-enforce-progress-block.yaml exists with single binary verify step.
